1. **Downy_mildew** — white parallel stripes on leaves, stunted seedlings, brown shredded lower leaves
2. **Maize_streak_virus** — streaking on leaves
3. **Stewarts_wilt** — pale streaks following leaf veins

Let me view reference images for these top candidates.
The Downy_mildew reference matches well — young seedlings in soil with white/pale striping on leaves. Let me view a couple more to confirm.

- **Test image**: Young corn seedling with pale/white parallel stripes along leaves, brown dead lower leaves, in soil setting
- **Downy_mildew** reference: Exactly matches — young seedlings in soil with white/pale parallel stripes alternating with green tissue, some lower leaves brown/dead
- **Maize_dwarf_mosaic_virus**: Shows narrow yellow streaks on more mature plants — less similar
- **Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma**: Shows reddish-purple discoloration on mature plants — doesn't match
- **Maize_chlorotic_dwarf_virus**: Shows vein banding/chlorosis on taller plants — less similar

The white parallel stripes running along the leaf length on this young seedling, combined with dead lower leaves, is the hallmark of Downy_mildew infection at the seedling stage.
